newsitem.title: USA: California's Yosemite Valley set to reopen.
newsitem.headline: California's Yosemite Valley set to reopen.

text.p: The most visited area of California's Yosemite National Park should reopen on March 15, two months after violent winter storms and floods forced park officials to close it down, officials said on Saturday.

Flooding in early January washed away roads and damaged bridges and cabins in the Yosemite Valley area, where the majority of park lodges and campgrounds are located. The scenic area has remained closed to visitors since then.

But if weather conditions remain favorable and if work crews complete temporary road and utility repairs on time, the National Park Service said people should be allowed to visit the Yosemite Valley area beginning March 15.
Some other parts of the huge park have already reopened.

The cost of storm and flood repairs at the national park has been estimated at $178 million, but park officials said the cost could climb once the snow has melted and crews are able to get into areas inaccessible during the winter.

The 760,000-acre (307,000-hectare) park, 150 miles (240 kms) southeast of San Francisco, is visited by four million hikers, climbers and sightseers each year, drawn by its towering mountains, high waterfalls and scenic wilderness.
